Tosafot on Bava Batra 106a:1:1.hebrew: הכי גרסי' פחות משתות הגיעו עד שתות ינכה - אבל ספרים דגרסי "פחות משתות הגיעו", יפרש רב יהודה "פיחת" עד שתות, ולא שתות בכלל, אע"ג דלא קתני "עד". וכענין זה יש בהזהב: "כמה תהא הסלע חסר ולא יהא בה אונאה", ובעי למימר "עד כמה". ולגירסא זו קשה, דקאמר בגמרא: ורב הונא ה"ק: פחות משתות ושתות עצמו הגיעו — הא להדיא אתיא מתני' כוותיה! וא"ת: בשלמא רב יהודה דאמר שתות כיתר משתות — ניחא; הא דלא תנן "שתות ינכה" — משום דה"א דיתר משתות מקחו בטל. אלא לרב הונא דאמר שתות כפחות משתות — ליתני "שתות הגיעו", וכ"ש פחות? וי"ל דנקט הכי ליתן טעם לדבר, דדבר פשוט הוא בפחות משתות, ואמר ממילא דשתות כפחות משתות. והשתא דאתינן להכי, לרב יהודה מצינו לשנויי סיפא כהאי גוונא:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 106a:1:1.english: So we read: "Less than a sixth, he is entitled to [the difference]; up to a sixth, he deducts" - But as for the texts that read "less than a sixth, he is entitled to [the difference]," Rav Yehudah would explain "he reduced" as meaning up to a sixth, but not including the sixth itself, even though [the Mishnah] does not state "up to." And similar to this there is in [the chapter] HaZahav: "How much may a sela be deficient so that there is no overcharge in it?" — where he wanted to say "up to how much." But according to this reading, there is a difficulty, because the Gemara says: "And Rav Huna, this is what [the Mishnah] is saying: less than a sixth, and a sixth itself, he is entitled to [the difference]" — [but] then the Mishnah explicitly accords with him! And if you say: Granted, according to Rav Yehudah, who says that a sixth is like more than a sixth, it is fine; the reason we do not learn "a sixth, he deducts" is because one might have thought that with more than a sixth the sale is void. But according to Rav Huna, who says that a sixth is like less than a sixth, let [the Mishnah] teach "a sixth, he is entitled to [the difference]," and all the more so less than a sixth? And one can answer: [The Mishnah] phrased it this way in order to give the reason for the matter, since it is obvious in the case of less than a sixth, and it said, by implication, that a sixth is like less than a sixth. And now that we have arrived at this, according to Rav Yehudah as well we can explain the latter clause in a similar manner:

Tosafot on Bava Batra 106a:5:1.hebrew: ה"ג ולטעמיך הא הגיעו קתני אלא כשום הדיינין ולא כשום הדיינין כו' - והכי פירושו: אמר לך רב הונא: אדמקשית לי, תסייעני מדקתני "הגיעו", דמשמע דשתות כפחות משתות. אלא הא דקתני "כשום הדיינין" — לאו משום דליהוי כיתר על שתות, אלא "כשום הדיינין" לשתות, דכמו ששיעורו התם כמו כן שיעורו כאן; לאפוקי שלא שיערו ברובע לסאה, כמו בהן חסר הן יתר. ורב יהודה דאותיב מינה לרב הונא, משמע ליה דהכי קתני: פיחת עד שתות או הותיר עד שתות, הרי הוא כשום הדיינין והגיעו, דהא בשום הדיינין נמי עד שתות הגיעו, אבל שתות ויתר על שתות לא הגיעו:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 106a:5:1.english: So we read: "And according to your reasoning, it teaches 'it reaches him'! Rather, [it means] 'like the assessment of the judges' and not 'like the assessment of the judges,' etc." - And this is its explanation: Rav Huna said to you: Instead of raising a difficulty against me, you should support me from the fact that it teaches "it reaches him," which implies that a sixth is like less than a sixth. Rather, as for that which it teaches "like the assessment of the judges" — it is not because it should be like an excess of more than a sixth; rather, "like the assessment of the judges" [applies] to a sixth, for just as its measure there [in the judges' assessment] is [up to a sixth], so too its measure here is the same; this is to exclude [the possibility] that they did not measure it by a quarter per se'ah, as in [the case of] "a hin short, a hin over." And Rav Yehuda, who raised the objection from it against Rav Huna, understands that it teaches as follows: If he fell short by up to a sixth, or exceeded by up to a sixth, it is like the assessment of the judges, and it reaches him, for in the assessment of the judges as well, up to a sixth it reaches him, but a sixth and more than a sixth does not reach him:
